newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Tension grips Pakistani city after mosque killings.
newsitem.headline: Tension grips Pakistani city after mosque killings.

text.p: The central Pakistani city of Multan came to a near standstill on Tuesday as residents mourned 21 worshippers killed in an attack on a mosque, witnesses said.
"There is a complete strike in the city and traffic is thin," one witness said. "Heavy contingents of police have been posted at sensitive points to keep watch."
Unidentified gunmen sprayed automatic gunfire at the dawn prayer congregation at the Sunni Moslem Al-Khair mosque in the city's Mumtazabad district on Monday, killing 21 and wounding many more.

The attack followed the murder of a militant Shi'ite leader in Bahawalpur, 95 km (60 miles) south of Multan, on Sunday. Gunmen killed another hardline Shi'ite leader in Bahawalpur on Monday, hours after the mosque shooting.
Troops in armoured carriers were deployed around Al-Khair mosque to quell unrest on Monday, but police replaced them overnight.
"Police are guarding the Imambargah (Shi'ite mosque) about 200 yards (metres) from Al-Khair mosque," a witness said, adding that many people had stayed at home fearing more violence.
The Milli Yekjehti Council, an alliance of religious parties including Sunni and Shi'ite groups, was due to hold a protest rally near the district courts later on Tuesday.
Newspapers said angry crowds had prevented National Assembly (lower house) speaker Yousaf Raza Gilani, who comes from Multan, from joining funeral prayers for the mosque victims on Monday.
A militant Sunni group has accused the Shi'ite Tehrik-e-Jafria Pakistan (TJP) of carrying out the mosque attack. The TJP has denied the charge.
"I am sure that it was the TJP men who killed the innocent worshippers," Tariq Madni, a Karachi-based spokesman for the Sipah-i-Shahaba Pakistan (SSP), said on Monday.
TJP chief Allama Sajid Naqvi denounced the attack. "Firing on worshippers is a worst kind of terrorism and we strongly condemn it," he said in a statement.
Sunni and Shi'ite militants have waged a bloody vendetta in Pakistan for several years. Shi'ites make up about 15 percent of the country's 130 million people, most of whom are Sunnis.
